newsitem.title: UK: UK Tory Party says ad campaign cost under 7 mln.
newsitem.headline: UK Tory Party says ad campaign cost under 7 mln.

text.p: Britain's Conservative Party on Tuesday said its newest advertising blitz cost far less than the seven-million pound figure reported by some media.
Other estimates have put the ad campaign at five million pounds.

"One figure is seven million pounds, which is far greater than the actual amount spent on advertising," one Tory source said. The seven million pound figure fails to distinguish between advertising and other campaign costs, such as direct mail promotions and campaigning, the source said.

Tory sources declined to detail the amount spent on the combined poster and press advertising campaign, reportedly the most expensive political campaign ever. The ads, which were launched on Monday, feature a series of five black and white photos, highlighted by a red teardrop falling from the eye of one person in each ad and red lettering. The ads all play on fears of what a Labour government would actually do.

The "tears" theme of the ads pressaged the message hammered at by Prime Minister John Major in a press conference Tuesday morning. Major, in the first of a series of presidential-style press conferences, said: "We have a choice economically between smiles and tears. I hope and believe when the election comes that people will choose the smiles and avoid the tears.

The five ads, designed by M&C Saatchi, the Tory Party's longtime advertising agency, play on five themes summed up in the ads' headlines: New Labour, New Failure; New Labour, New Mortgage Risk; New Labour, New Job Losses; New Labour, New Price Rises; and New Labour, New Taxes.
Although the ads have been subject to widespread criticism in the press for their negative tone, Tory sources insisted it is not a negative campaign.
"We don't think it's a particularly negative campaign," one source said. "It's a campaign that offers a choice. We're offering a choice between two futures. ...
"What we've said is Labour will say anything ... to win," the source said. "They won't give you any details, and we're trying to say that's leaving people dangerously in the dark.
The ad campaign is heavily weighted to posters, favoured for their street presence and ability to encourage supporters and activists, a Tory source said.

The Conservative Party, which continues to sharply lag Labour in public opinion polls by some 20 points, continues to insist that it will win the next general election. The general election must be held by May 22, and Major has vowed to call the election by May 1.
"We'll see the effectiveness of the ads on election days when we win," a Tory source said.
